text: Two studies examine mitotic and embryonic patterning. Asp, a 220K microtubule-associated protein at the centrosome face contacting spindle microtubules, is the Mr 220K Polo kinase substrate; Polo phosphorylates Asp in vitro, generating an MPM2 epitope. Polo and Asp co-immunoprecipitate in a 25–38S complex. polo-derived embryo extracts cannot restore aster nucleation in salt-stripped centrosomes, rescued by phosphorylated Asp or active Polo. asp mutants show bipolar spindles with disorganized broad poles and abnormal γ-tubulin distribution; polo1 aspE3 double mutants synergize. Separately, quadruple knockdown of ADMP and BMP2/4/7 in Xenopus eliminates self-regulation, causing ubiquitous neural induction. ADMP, activated at low BMP in the Spemann organizer, signals via ALK-2 and is dorsally inhibited by Chordin; ventral antagonists Sizzled and Bambi refine pattern. Graft transplants show both poles act as signaling centers.
